help.title: Help & Documentation
help.subtitle: Getting started, ChordPro format, import guides, and more.

start.title: Getting Started
start.intro: ChordCrew is an offline-first PWA for managing ChordPro songs and setlists. All data is stored on your device — no internet required during worship.
start.step1: Go to Library to see your songs. Tap + (top-right) to create a new song.
start.step2: Use the Editor to write ChordPro content. The right panel previews the rendering live.
start.step3: Open a song in Viewer to transpose, change columns, or enter Performance mode.
start.step4: Build a Setlist and present it in full-screen mode with pedal navigation.
start.install: To install as a PWA, use "Add to Home Screen" in your browser (Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android / desktop).

chordpro.title: ChordPro Format
chordpro.intro: ChordPro places chords inline above lyrics using square brackets.

chordswiki.title: Migrating from chords.wiki
chordswiki.intro: Export your library from chords.wiki: Settings → Export → Library backup (JSON).
chordswiki.step2: Drop the <mono>.json</mono> file onto the upload area (or click to browse).
chordswiki.step3: If songs already exist you can Skip or Overwrite them.
chordswiki.step4: Books, songs, and setlists are all imported in one step.
chordswiki.flagged: Songs with filename-style titles (e.g. my_song.cho) are flagged in the import summary for cleanup.

opensong.title: Migrating from OpenSong
opensong.intro: OpenSong stores songs as XML files (no extension). ChordCrew can import them directly.
opensong.step2: Select one or more OpenSong XML files (multi-select is supported).
opensong.step3: ChordCrew converts positional chord alignment to ChordPro inline format.
opensong.step4: Key, tempo, time signature, CCLI, and copyright are extracted automatically — including when they appear as inline text in the lyrics (Key - G | Tempo - 72).
opensong.sections: Section types are mapped: V → Verse, C → Chorus, B → Bridge, P → Pre-Chorus, T → Tag.

performance.title: Performance Mode & Pedal Navigation
performance.intro: Enter Performance mode from any song's Viewer toolbar (↕ icon). The screen stays on and all sync is disabled.
performance.arrows: Arrow Right / Left — advance / go back one column
performance.longRight: Long-press Right — skip to next song in setlist
performance.longLeft: Long-press Left — back to start of current song
performance.tap: Tap left/right half — same as arrow keys (touch)
performance.pedal: Compatible pedal: PageFlip Cicada V7 in Mode 2 (emits Left/Right Arrow). Reassign pedal keys in Settings → Pedal.
performance.setlist: In a setlist, reaching the last column of a song advances to the next song automatically.

midi.title: MIDI: Kemper Rig & Tempo
midi.intro: ChordCrew can switch your Kemper Profiler to the right rig and tempo whenever you open a song (Viewer or Performance mode) — e.g. via a CME WIDI Master Bluetooth adapter plugged into the Kemper's MIDI In.
midi.step1: Connect the MIDI adapter to your device (macOS: Audio MIDI Setup → Bluetooth; Android: a BLE-MIDI connector app; iPad/iPhone: inside the Web MIDI Browser app — see below).
midi.step2: In Settings → MIDI, switch on Send MIDI on song change, allow MIDI access, pick the output and use Test.
midi.step3: Give each song a rig — the editor shows a Rig field once MIDI is on:
midi.example:
{tempo: 72}          ← tempo, as before
{x_kemper_rig: 17}   ← Program Change 17 (Browser Mode assignment)
{x_kemper_rig: 6.2}  ← Performance 6, Slot 2 (Performance Mode)
midi.allRigs: All rigs at once: Settings → MIDI → Edit the rigs of all songs opens a table of every song's rig and tempo. After reorganising performances on the Kemper, use Replace rig: e.g. 6.* → 8.* moves every song from performance 6 to 8 (keeping the slot), 6.2 → 8.3 changes one rig.
midi.switches: Rig & tempo switches: turn off Send rig change to keep one rig for every song (the songs' rig settings are ignored); turn off Send tempo to leave the tempo alone. Exact sets the BPM directly; Tap sends four tap-tempo presses instead. The Kemper's MIDI channel is Omni by default, so channel 1 works.
midi.slots: Switching slots during a song: a slot with its own stored tempo replaces the song tempo when you step on it. To keep the song tempo, switch Tempo Enable off in the Rig settings of those slots on the Kemper and store the performance.
midi.ipad: iPad/iPhone: Safari has no Web MIDI. Install the free Web MIDI Browser app, connect the WIDI there and open chordcrew.app in it — the WIDI is listed as output "Bluetooth". The app keeps its own copy of your library, so sync first. Elsewhere use Chrome or Edge (Android, macOS, Windows).

teams.title: Teams & Shared Libraries
teams.intro: Teams let you share songs and setlists with your worship band. Requires Google Sign-In.
teams.step1: Go to Teams and create a team.
teams.step2: Invite members by their Google email address.
teams.step3: They accept via the notification banner at the top of the screen.
teams.owner: Owner — full admin: invite, remove, change roles, edit everything
teams.share: To share your personal songs: select songs in Library → Organize → Copy/Move to team.

sync.title: Sync & Backup
sync.intro: Sync is manual only — tap the sync badge in the sidebar or Settings → Sync Now.
sync.yellow: Yellow — unsynced changes or updates available
sync.backup: To back up your library: go to Import → Export to download a chords.wiki-compatible JSON file. Re-import it on any device.

curation.title: Library Curation
curation.intro: The Curation page (sidebar) helps you keep your library tidy.
curation.duplicates: Duplicates — finds songs with identical or very similar titles (≥ 75% word overlap). Click Edit to open the song.
curation.errors: Parse Errors — scans all songs for unclosed braces or brackets. Click Fix → to jump to the editor.
curation.export: Export CSV — downloads all song metadata (title, artist, key, tempo, tags, CCLI, copyright, book) as a CSV file.

blank.problem: Song renders blank or shows "Parse Error"
blank.solution: Open the song in the Editor — the Preview panel highlights parse errors with line numbers. Use Fix → to jump to the problem line.

orange.problem: Chords show in orange in the editor
orange.solution: Orange underline = unknown chord name. Check the spelling — ChordCrew only recognises standard notation (A–G, no German H).

importFails.problem: Import fails with "Not a chords.wiki library-backup file"
importFails.solution: Make sure you exported the full library backup (not individual song exports) from chords.wiki.

syncGrey.solution: The app is offline or Firebase is not configured. Sync requires an internet connection and a valid Firebase project.

wakeLock.problem: Wake lock not working in Performance mode
wakeLock.solution: Wake Lock API requires the page to be served over HTTPS. It is also not supported in Firefox.
